items.title: Fewer empty tankers heading to the Gulf
items.summary: TankerTrackers.com estimates the combined capacity of VLCCs and Suezmaxes ballasting toward the Middle East is down about 40% since end-August, with some owners declining to transit Hormuz and loading from shuttle tankers in the Gulf of Oman. A tighter supply of empty ships would tend to support rates after recent declines.

items.title: VLCC rates down 64% from October record
items.summary: Baltic Exchange data show Gulf of Oman–China VLCC freight at about WS 308 on Nov 13, against a record WS 841 on Oct 8. Oil prices have fallen roughly 20% in November on hopes of de-escalation.

items.title: Crude tanker freight corrects; US Gulf quiet
items.summary: Breakwave's bi-weekly report says crude freight has pulled back sharply from October highs, with more VLCCs ballasting east and firming prompt tonnage around Fujairah and Yanbu. It describes the US Gulf as subdued and notes Saudi East-West pipeline flows have resumed.

items.title: Oil market moves into surplus; European diesel near $170/bbl
items.summary: The IEA said on Nov 13 that supply is outpacing demand for the first time since the war began. Saudi output reached 10.5m b/d in October, China's crude imports fell about 15% y/y to 9.9m b/d, and US weekly crude output passed 14m b/d.

items.title: Jones Act waiver runs to Feb 14, 2027
items.summary: CBP confirmed the third 90-day extension of the waiver first issued Mar 17, effective Nov 16; cargo must load by 11:59 PM ET on Feb 14. Approvals remain voyage-by-voyage after a MARAD survey for US-flag tonnage; the American Maritime Partnership and OMSA want it ended.

items.title: EU sanctions target shadow-fleet managers and insurers
items.summary: The EU listed 113 individuals and entities, including Dubai-based Lidoil DMCC and several ship managers, Moscow insurer Balance Insurance and Petersburg Oil Terminal. Nearly 50 Russian banks were also added; measures include asset freezes and travel bans.

items.title: SwissChemGas orders two VLACs at Hengli
items.summary: SwissChemGas has joined the current wave of very large ammonia carrier orders with a pair from China's Hengli. Only the headline was reviewed; price and delivery dates were not confirmed.

items.title: LPG tanker Tara Gas abandoned after two strikes in Hormuz
items.summary: UKMTO reported a first attack around 1900 UTC on Nov 16 about 7 nm north of Khasab, followed by a second strike; both caused fires. The 25 crew abandoned ship; India says 21 nationals reached Khasab, two are hospitalised and one is missing. A separate outbound tanker was hit at 0558 UTC with all crew safe; responsibility is not established.

items.title: LPG tanker Gas Husky sinks off Bulgaria
items.summary: The Liberian-flag vessel, carrying 3,400 t of LPG, sank about 50 miles east of Byala on Nov 17; all 19 crew were rescued and no pollution was reported. The cause is not yet known. Diaplous counts at least 17 ships attacked off Bulgaria and Romania since mid-July.

items.title: Wheat carrier capsizes off Bulgaria after reported drone strike
items.summary: The Somali-flagged BETUL 8, carrying about 3,000 t of wheat from Tulcea to Egypt, capsized about 40 nm southeast of Cape Kaliakra. All 12 crew were rescued; the crew reported two sea drones, but responsibility has not been confirmed.

items.title: New Orleans riverboat collision: tanker steering loss under review
items.summary: Preliminary data indicate the tanker Atlantic Asphalt had its rudder to starboard after a steering casualty and struck the berthed American Heritage about two minutes later on Nov 13; all 190 aboard survived, 32 went to hospital. The NTSB has not determined cause and had flagged Mississippi berth risks in 1998.

items.title: Armed skiff approaches tanker 430 nm east of Socotra
items.summary: UKMTO logged a possible mothership and a skiff with four armed people and a ladder approaching a tanker on Nov 16. There was no boarding or gunfire; UKMTO classes it as suspicious activity, and JMIC rates Somali piracy risk as moderate.

items.title: DHL: over 10% of container fleet tied up in congestion
items.summary: DHL estimates about 3.6m TEU is held up by port congestion and says the return to Suez may take another 6–12 months, with schedule reliability weak into 2027. Some Gulf gateways have berth delays over two weeks.

items.title: Gemini moves three more Asia–Europe loops back to Suez
items.summary: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd will switch AE2 (from Dec 4), AE3 (Dec 20) and AE1 (Jan 14, 2027) from the Cape route to the Suez Canal, following earlier moves of AE5, AE11, AE12, ME2 and ME1.

items.title: Trump in Asia for ASEAN summit, then talks with Xi and Putin
items.summary: The President left Washington on Nov 16 with Secretary of State Rubio and Treasury Secretary Bessent for the 49th ASEAN summit in the Philippines and a China visit, and said a meeting with Kim Jong Un is possible. No summit outcomes had been reported at publication.

items.title: Third US aircraft carrier reaches the Middle East
items.summary: A US official confirmed the USS Theodore Roosevelt has arrived in the region, giving the administration more options in the Iran conflict.

items.title: EU says Russia is slowing Ukraine peace talks
items.summary: EU governments said Moscow is drawing out negotiations while striking power plants and other infrastructure ahead of winter.

items.title: Russia reports intercepting 1,336 Ukrainian drones
items.summary: Russia's Defense Ministry said on Nov 16 it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones, the highest figure it has claimed since the 2022 invasion. The number has not been independently verified.

items.title: US tightens limits on China's access to advanced AI chips
items.summary: The administration announced new rules to close gaps that had allowed advanced AI chips to reach China, ahead of the President's meeting with Xi.

items.title: COP31: fossil-fuel transition coalition proceeds without Colombia
items.summary: At the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey, a group of countries plans to present new national plans to move away from fossil fuels, despite the withdrawal of Colombia, its original sponsor.

items.title: Texans 3–6 host Colts Thursday
items.summary: Houston lost 27–24 at Cleveland on Nov 15 and sits second in the AFC South, behind Jacksonville (7–2) and ahead of Indianapolis (3–7) and Tennessee (1–8). Next: Colts at NRG Stadium, Thu Nov 19, 7:15 PM CT (Prime Video).

items.title: Broncos 7–2 host Raiders Sunday
items.summary: Denver, off its bye, last beat Carolina 26–21 on Nov 8 and is tied with Kansas City (7–2) atop the AFC West, second on tiebreaker; Las Vegas is 4–6. Next: Raiders at home, Sun Nov 22, 3:25 PM CT (CBS).

items.title: ATP Finals: Fils beats Jodar; Shelton–Zverev later Tuesday
items.summary: Arthur Fils came from a set down to beat Rafael Jodar 4–6, 6–2, 6–2 for his first Finals win (1–1); Jodar, who took two medical timeouts, is 0–2. Shelton (1–0) meets No. 1 Zverev (1–0) later on Nov 17, with a semi-final place at stake; Fils plays Zverev on Thursday.

items.title: ATP Finals: Alcaraz and Medvedev open with wins
items.summary: In the Ivan Lendl Group on Nov 16, Alcaraz beat Frances Tiafoe 6–2, 6–2 in 69 minutes and Medvedev beat Flavio Cobolli 7–6(4), 6–3. Zverev and Shelton won their John McEnroe Group openers on Nov 15; the event runs through Nov 22 in Turin.

items.title: Andreeva wins WTA Finals, rises to No. 2
items.summary: Mirra Andreeva beat Elina Svitolina 7–5, 6–3 in the final, after going through the round robin without dropping a set. She moves past Aryna Sabalenka to No. 2, 293 points behind No. 1 Elena Rybakina.
